sections.skill: Share less by minimizing and redacting details

questions.prompt: What does data minimization mean?

choices.text: Deleting all your files every day
Sharing only what the task needs
Making your files as small as possible
Sharing everything so the tool understands

questions.correct_answer: Sharing only what the task needs
questions.intro: DATA MINIMIZATION means sharing only what a task actually needs. Before pasting, ask: "Would the result be just as good without this detail?" Often it would. To get help rewording a letter, the tool does not need real names, account numbers or addresses. REDACTION removes or masks details: delete them, replace them with placeholders like [NAME] or [ACCOUNT], or use made-up but realistic values. Keep a note of what you replaced so you can put the real details back afterward. Minimizing protects you and others even when a tool's privacy settings are good.

sections.skill: Compare minimizing with packing for a day hike

questions.prompt: What do you pack for a day hike?

choices.text: Everything you own
Nothing at all
What the trip needs
Your passport and jewelry

questions.correct_answer: What the trip needs
questions.intro: For a day hike you pack water, a snack, a map and a jacket: what the trip needs. You do not bring your passport, your jewelry and your whole wallet, because if you drop the bag on the trail, everything in it is at risk. Sharing information with an AI tool is similar. Bring only what the task needs. For anything sensitive that you must refer to, use a stand-in, like writing "[my bank]" instead of the real account details.

questions.prompt: Why leave the passport at home?

If the bag is lost, it is at risk

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: Sam drew black boxes over account numbers in a file, but the text could still be copied. What happened?

choices.text: The redaction worked perfectly
The boxes only covered the text visually
Black boxes delete text in every file type
The numbers were never there

questions.correct_answer: The boxes only covered the text visually
questions.intro: Redaction can fail in subtle ways. Blacking out text in some files only covers it visually while the text remains underneath; screenshots of a redacted area or retyping are safer. Placeholders must be consistent: if [PERSON A] becomes [PERSON B] halfway through, the tool may treat them as two people. And over-redacting can remove context the task truly needs, such as a person's role ("the manager") or a date range. Replace identifying details with meaningful placeholders instead of deleting everything.
questions.feedback: Visual covers may leave text underneath.
